Both require manual Python reimplementation - the MAMA indicator logic and the trade management functions (BuyPositionClose, SellPositionClose, BuyPositionOpen, SellPositionOpen, LoadHistory, CIsNewBar, GlobalVariableDel_) must be reverse-engineered or reimplemented.

other_exits: Long position closed when MAMA crosses below FAMA (Ma1 < Ma2 on bar 1) and BuyPosClose is enabled
Short position closed when MAMA crosses above FAMA (Ma1 > Ma2 on bar 1) and SellPosClose is enabled

params.description: MM=-0.1 means fixed 0.1 lot; positive values represent deposit share fraction

position_sizing.conditional_logic: If MM < 0, use |MM| as fixed lot size; if MM > 0, use MM as fraction of deposit

custom_logic_notes: MAMA (MESA Adaptive Moving Average) by John Ehlers - adaptive MA that adjusts speed based on cycle phase. Uses two lines: MAMA (fast adaptive) and FAMA (slow adaptive). Entry on crossover of MAMA above/below FAMA on completed bar (SignalBar=1). The crossover detection compares bar[1] vs bar[0] of the indicator buffers: long when Ma1[1]>Ma2[1] AND Ma1[0]<Ma2[0] (MAMA was below FAMA on prior bar, now above), short vice versa. TradeAlgorithms.mqh provides CIsNewBar class for new bar detection, LoadHistory for history loading, and wrapper functions for position open/close with signal time tracking. Signal time is recorded as last bar datetime + timeframe shift, likely used for order expiration or slippage control in the trade library.
python_conversion_notes: Primary challenge: reimplementing MAMA_Optim indicator in Python. MESA Adaptive Moving Average algorithm is well-documented (Ehlers 'Cybernetic Analysis for Stocks and Futures'). The indicator takes FastLimit and SlowLimit params and outputs two buffers (MAMA and FAMA). Secondary challenge: TradeAlgorithms.mqh functions need simplified Python equivalents - position sizing (MM negative=lot, positive=deposit fraction), market order execution with SL/TP in points, and new-bar detection. Crossover logic is straightforward: detect when MAMA crosses above FAMA for longs, below for shorts. SignalBar=1 means use the previous completed bar for decisions. The trade library's UpSignalTime/DnSignalTime tracking appears to be for order expiration management and can be simplified to bar-based entry in backtest. Point-based SL (1000) and TP (2000) values need symbol-specific pip/point conversion.
